name: Dot Field Showreel
tagline: Viewfinder HUD, one-second colour cuts, kinetic type and a dot field that ripples on cue.
description: Motion-designer showreel style for portfolios, studio reels and 'what we can do' intros. A camera-viewfinder HUD (corner brackets, timecode, scene labels) frames rapid scenes: tumbling letters with a glitch slice, outline-stack type on electric blue, a frame counter on orange, a grid of dots rippling in orange and blue waves, and a lime end card.
transitions: hard cut with full background colour switch every ~1–2s
glitch slice: two clipped colour copies jump sideways for 4 frames
textAnimations: letters tumble in from above with alternating ±28° rotation
outline rows slide in from opposite sides around one filled word
frame counter ticks 0240 → 0261 with a progress bar
dot field ripples via grid stagger from centre, then from a corner
end word expands from scaleY 0.1 with outline echoes

rhythm.notes: Five scenes in 7.5s. Short scenes ~1–1.2s, the dot field gets ~2.2s to show two waves.

guide:
- Keep the viewfinder HUD on top of every scene: four corner brackets, reel label, frame timecode, scene name, author. Flip it from light to dark on light backgrounds.
- Cut hard between near-black, electric blue #2b45ff, orange #ff5a1f and lime #d4ff3a; never two adjacent scenes in the same colour.
- Each scene shows one technique and names it in the HUD (Type, Intent, Timing, Systems, Move).
- Type: Archivo Black for the hero word, Instrument Serif italic for small connecting words, outline copies for echoes.
- Dot fields are a fixed grid animated only with grid staggers (from centre, from a corner) so the motion reads as a system.
- Drive counters and HUD text from one clock tween's onUpdate so seeking stays deterministic.
